newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Southcorp sees strong earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Southcorp sees strong earnings growth.

text.p: Vintner and appliance manufacturer Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it expected its current profit growth trend to continue and that strong earnings growth could be maintained for the balance of the year ending June 30, 1997.
"Southcorp's current profit growth trend is expected to continue," Southcorp said in its first half results statement.

"This would be driven from further efficiency gains in Southcorp Appliances in both Australia and the United States, together with the introduction of new products and increased demand from the upturn in the housing cycle, which is expected in the September 1997 quarter," Southcorp said.

Earlier Southcorp reported a 22.3 percent rise in net profit to A$64.92 million for the first half year. Pre-abnormal net profit rose 16.6 percent to A$62.9 million. Southcorp set an unchanged interim dividend of 8.25 cents per share.

"The result, which was a direct outcome of Southcorp's strategy to drive profit by targeting investment to growth businesses and managing costs, was particularly pleasing, given flat economic conditions in Australia," Southcorp said.
Sales fell 0.5 percent to A$1.297 billion from A$1.304 billion in the previous comparable year.

Pre-tax and interest earnings from Southcorp Wines rose 14.3 percent to A$54.45 million on a sales rise of 14.6 percent to A$280.1 million. Pre-tax and interest earnings from Southcorp Packaging rose 0.4 percent to A$64.20 million on a sales fall of 2.6 percent to A$558.31 million.
Pre-tax and interest earnings from Southcorp Appliances rose 29.1 percent to A$18.84 million while sales fell 5.6 percent to A$458.98 million.
"The strong performance at Southcorp Wines is expected to continue with profit growth enhanced by increased red wine availability and grape supply from new vineyards," it said.

"While the benefits of the extra vineyard production would begin to flow in 1997/98, the full benefit would take a few more years. In the meantime the June half performance would be constrained by the lack of availabilty of red wine from the poor 1995 vintage."
Southcorp said its Packaging unit would gain from the growth offshore and from new contracts in Australia.
"This will include further expansion of PET (polyethelene terephthalate plastic containers) in Asia together with growth from the U.S. packaging business," it said.
"Directors are confident that, provided there is no significant downturn in the Australian and U.S. economies, strong earnings growth can be maintained for the balance of the year."
Southcorp Holdings shares were up one cent at A$4.57 at 1.45 p.m. (0245 GMT).
